chapter_title: Concerning the Cross of Light: [...] trample upon

14.content: they will be able to diss

spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

---

**¶7**

For the divine life captive in natural states suffers in just this way. When falsity and evil take hold of the external faculties of the mind, and the will grows unresponsive, and the interior life is in anguish, and there is suffering throughout from the corruption that pervades it — then the soul seeks divine wisdom to restore it, to strengthen the will toward good. And divine wisdom corrects, attends to, and restores wholeness [GAP-1] from the falsity and evil that had risen up against it. Thus the soul reflects upon this process.

---

**¶8**

[GAP-2] One who possesses interior wisdom comes, knowing the doctrinal truths proper to a skilled healer of the spirit. If such a one shall accomplish the reformation of the soul whom he [GAP-3] has undertaken to restore, he speaks over that soul the truths of doctrine that he knows, and he even disciplines with his power every external faculty of the mind. The soul suffering under falsity recognizes that this discipline is applied so that reformation might be accomplished — that it is not done from any hostility held against it. Rather, all that divine wisdom does, it does so that it may bring about the restoration of the external mind. And it expels [GAP-4] the falsity and the suffering, pressing upon the outer faculties to bring about this spiritual benefit. The soul under correction can harbor no resentment nor opposition against this divine wisdom that disciplines it. It cannot turn against wisdom in hostility, because it perceives that all this is done for its good.

---

**¶9**

However, should falsity from evil come and press upon the soul in hostility — the soul may resist, repel, and refuse it. For it perceives that this assault comes from enmity; and as evil strikes out of wanton desire, it heaps further corruption upon the existing spiritual disease.

---

**¶10**

And again, so it is with the divine life captive in natural states, whether in the external mind or in the divine good dispersed throughout all of creation. Should you progress upon it along the path of spiritual life, should you press upon the scattered divine good, it takes no reckoning against you in resentment or indignation. For it perceives that [GAP-5] you advance upon it for liberation and restoration, to proclaim the truth on its behalf. [GAP-6] You journey because of it, to reveal its interior spiritual realities. Also, the suffering imposed upon the foundational truths of faith, which you have pressed down, does not pertain to sin but is directed toward the triumph of good over evil. And again, because of this nothing shall be lost to you on account of the suffering of foundational truths and your spiritual labor; rather, all of it accumulates toward the liberation of the divine life within.

---

**¶12**

Rather, the communication that destroys spiritual life is this: should a person utter a declaration for the sake of destroying the understanding of truth in another, or for destroying the affections for good, or for [GAP-7] the destruction of perceptions of truth and of the divine good dispersed in creation — the false word, and the word born of self-love, and the bitter word, or a word of hellish envy and [GAP-8] malice alone, or a word of accusation that someone spreads against his fellow — this is the communication that destroys [GAP-9] spiritual life. Should a person utter it, it pertains to sin, because he has brought forth from it the spirits of evil [GAP-10] concerning this [GAP-11] the one who lives in good, or [GAP-12] all those states which I have proclaimed, in order that [GAP-13] his speech might bind the soul in bondage — because anyone who would [GAP-14] bind his speech to spiritual bondage — and again, he [GAP-15] at the time of his departure from the body, they will bind him in the very state in which he has bound his [GAP-16] fellow.

---

**¶14**

He is like this: a wise divine healer who turns back [GAP-17] the corruption of the soul. As a deep spiritual wound exists within the external mind, he makes an incision [GAP-18] into this soul suffering under falsity, through his wisdom, [GAP-19] he [GAP-20] addresses this wound, and he cuts into it. After this [GAP-21] he applies the truths that dissolve falsity upon it, so that they may dissolve the corruption. He may pierce it with the sharp power of natural truth, and he casts the corruption out from the soul by means of those dissolving truths. And the wound is purified from the burning of self-love. After these things, he applies the gentle goods of charity [GAP-22] and the spiritual wound closes and is made whole. The soul that was ill shall render [GAP-23] gratitude, and shall not [GAP-24] resist; he [GAP-25] shall not generate resentment in his will against divine wisdom — because he perceives that it is accomplishing his benefit and his restoration. After the severance of evil that wisdom may perform, and the purification by holy ardor that it may carry out, the soul shall even render reciprocal love to the source of its healing. It gives its gratitude and is conjoined to divine wisdom in friendship through the whole of its life.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: because the living soul is like this. As a person, if a disease will take hold of his limbs, and his heart [is sl]ow, his soul distressed, and he has pain in his disease. He seeks after a doctor to cure him, to make him strong of heart. And he cures, attends to, and gives him health [from] the disease that has risen up against him. So he thinks about this.

[And] a wise person comes, knowing the formulas proper to a skilled doctor. If he shall achieve a healing of the one whom he [has undertaken to cure, and he accomplishes] it, he recites over him the formulas that he knows, and he even tramples with his foot upon all his limbs! That person, who is ill, knows that this person is trampling upon him so that he might achieve a healing; rather, not doing this to him out of some enmity he had against him beforehand. Instead, all that he does, he does to him that he might make a healing of his body. And he expels [the] disease and the pain, trampling upon him to occasion this benefit. That person, who is ill, he can bear no anger nor hatred against this doctor, who tramples upon him. He can not hate him out of enmity, because he knows that he does this to him to his benefit.

However, should someone come and trample upon him in enmity; he may hate, prevent and not permit him! For he knows that he tramples upon him in enmity; and as he strikes out of a wanton whim, he piles another illness upon his disease.

Again, this too is the case with the living soul; whether in the earth, or in the Cross of Light. Should you walk along upon it on the path, should you trample the Cross, it may take no reckoning against you in anger nor wrath. For it knows that [you] walk upon it for relief and healing, to proclaim on its behalf. [You] walk because of it, to reveal its mysteries. Also, the distress of the bones, which you have oppressed, befits not sin, but is set towards the victory. Again, because of this nothing will be lost for you due to the distress of the bones and your toil; rather, it all accumulates to the relief (of the soul).

Rather, the word that wounds is this: should a person utter a saying for the sake of the murder of a person, or the murder of animals, or for [the sake of] the murder of trees and the Cross of Light, the lying word and the wrathful and the bitter, or a word of envy and [malice] only, or a word of accusation, which someone will spread against his brother; this is the [wor]d that wounds [the living soul]. Should the person utter it, it befits [si]n; because [he has br]ought forth from it the demons [who speak] concerning this [against] the righteous person, or [against] all of them, which I have proclaimed, in order that [he might bind] his word to the fetter; because anyone who would [bind] his word to the fetter. And again, he [at the time of] his coming forth, they will bind him in the place wherein he has bound his [brother].

[He is li]ke this, a wise doctor who might turn back [a sick person from] his disease. As a wound is in his body, he cuts [into] this person who is ill, in his wisdom, [until] he [uncovers] this wound, and he cuts it. After these things [are done] and he places the soluble drugs upon it, so that [they will be able to diss]olve. He might incise it with the iron, and he casts it out [f]rom him, with the soluble drugs. And the wound is purified [fr]om the fever. After these events, he shall place the soothing drugs [upon it] and it heals up. That person, who is ill, he shall give [his thanks] but he shall not [oppose him, and] he [shall not] generate anger in his heart against him; because he knows that he is making the aspect of his benefit and his healing. After the cut that he may make, and the cauterizing that he may do there, he shall even give rewards to the doctor! He gives his thanks and is a friend to him his whole life through.

fills.explanation: The preposition "from" correctly indicates the source of the disease being healed, matching the spiritual sense of restoring wholeness from falsity and evil.
The conjunction "And" naturally continues the narrative sequence from ¶7's reflection into the introduction of the wise doctor figure.

fills.fill: has undertaken to cure, and he accomplishes
fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "has undertaken to restore" — in the medical register, the doctor "has undertaken to cure" the patient, and "he accomplishes it" provides the referent for the resumptive "it" that follows, completing the conditional about achieving the healing.
The definite article "the" correctly introduces the already-mentioned disease, paralleling "the pain" that follows in the same clause.
The second-person "you" continues the direct address established in "Should you walk along upon it" and matches the spiritual reading's "you advance upon it."
The second-person "You" maintains the direct address pattern of the passage, beginning a new sentence about the hearer's journey on behalf of the living soul.
The phrase "the sake of" maintains the parallel construction with "for the sake of the murder of a person" earlier in the same sentence.
The spiritual reading specifies "malice" as the companion vice to envy, and it complements the list of harmful word-types (lying, wrathful, bitter) without redundancy.

The chapter's governing subject is "the living soul" (¶7, ¶10), and the spiritual reading says "destroys spiritual life" — in the Kephalaia's register, "the living soul" is the precise term for the spiritual life that the wounding word destroys.

The entire passage concerns harmful speech — lying words, words of accusation spread against one's brother — so the demons "brought forth" by such speech naturally "speak" (accuse, testify) concerning this against the righteous person, continuing the theme of destructive utterance.

The demons brought forth by harmful speech act "against" the righteous person — this hostile preposition connects "concerning this" to its target, matching the spiritual reading's sense of evil spirits working against the one who lives in good.
Parallel construction with GAP-11: "against the righteous person, or against all of them" — the harmful words and their demons operate against all the states of good that have been proclaimed.

The spiritual reading says "his speech might bind the soul in bondage," and the purpose clause "in order that he might bind his word to the fetter" directly states the binding intention, which is then restated in the next clause.
The spiritual reading says "bind his speech to spiritual bondage," and the sentence directly restates the preceding clause about fettering — "bind his word to the fetter" completes the parallelism.

The spiritual reading specifies "at the time of his departure from the body" — the temporal phrase "at the time of" connects to "his coming forth" (= departure from the body) to establish when the binding retribution occurs.

The text uses "brother" for one's fellow earlier in ¶12 ("which someone will spread against his brother"), and the spiritual reading confirms "fellow" — the Kephalaia's own term for this is "brother."

The spiritual reading says "turns back the corruption of the soul" — in the natural medical register, the doctor "turns back a sick person from his disease," redirecting the patient away from the corruption, which matches the healer-patient structure of ¶14.
The spiritual reading says "makes an incision into this soul" — the doctor "cuts into" the patient, which is the standard medical action of making an incision to reach a wound.
In the medical sequence, the doctor cuts into the patient "until" he uncovers the wound — "until" provides the temporal connector between the incision and the exposure of the wound.

The doctor cuts into the patient until he "uncovers" the wound, then cuts it out — this is the standard medical sequence of incision, exposure, and excision that the spiritual reading renders as "addresses."

The spiritual reading shows no additional action at this point — the gap is a brief transitional phrase completing "After these things are done, and he places the soluble drugs upon it," bridging the cutting to the application of dissolving medicines.
Directly parallels the earlier identical construction "he places the soluble drugs upon it" — the soothing drugs are likewise placed upon the wound.
The passage's own closing line uses the identical phrase "He gives his thanks," confirming the vocabulary; the spiritual reading correspondingly says "render gratitude."

The spiritual reading says "shall not resist," and the parallel in ¶8 ("He can bear no anger nor hatred... He can not hate him") establishes a double-negative pattern; "oppose him, and he shall not generate anger" maintains this structure.

The negative "shall not" correctly continues the parallel prohibition structure: "he shall not [oppose]... he shall not generate anger," matching the spiritual reading's emphasis on the soul not resisting divine wisdom.
